expected_effect: Recreating ad's container should end the log silence that has held since 20:59:11. Within roughly one JVM cold start (the previous one took ~17s from first line to 'listening on gRPC port' [tr_ce520f9e7393]) Loki on {namespace="astronomy-shop",pod=~"ad-..."} should show a fresh startup sequence followed by ordinary per-request ad lines carrying populated trace ids, and no further 'gRPC shutdown / JVM shutdown' line. Note the confirmation must be log-based: ad emits no trace-derived span metrics, so error-ratio and latency percentiles do not exist for it in Prometheus [tr_1c44b72de6bd], and Tempo held no ad spans at all [tr_2178f15d99cb] — if spans do reappear in Tempo after the restart that is a bonus signal, not a required one.
if_wrong: Three falsifiers. (1) No startup lines appear within five minutes — the container is not being scheduled, and the mechanism is at the orchestrator, not the process. (2) Startup lines appear and are followed within a minute or two by another JVM-driven graceful shutdown — something external is signalling ad to stop (the open question of what sent the 20:59:11 signal was never answered; no pod state, restart count, or exit code was retrieved), and repeating the restart will just churn. (3) ad logs resume and serve normally but product-catalog is still alerting — the causal link from ad to product-catalog was never shown (its unfiltered logs were never queried [tr_181fc5b26702], its span metrics do not exist [tr_f2b13604310b]), so a shared upstream trigger would remain live and this restart would have fixed a symptom.
risk: restart_service is not reversible. If the 20:59:11 stop was commanded by something still in force — an operator-driven teardown, a scheduler eviction, a supervisor — the recreate either fails or is undone, and we have spent the one irreversible action while learning less than a pod-state/exit-code query would have told us for free. If ad was in fact already restarted by the platform after 20:59:11 (unverified), this recreate interrupts a working process and causes a second, self-inflicted outage window. It also discards in-process state; for ad that is cache only, so the cost is a cold cache and slower first responses, not data. And it closes off post-mortem inspection of the stopped container's exit code.
blast_radius: One service for the duration of the recreate. This brief names only ad's outbound edge (ad → flagd), not its callers, so the inbound set is not fully enumerated here — operators should assume the services that render ads see connection-refused or reset during the recreate, and should check the frontend path specifically. flagd sees ad's flag-evaluation traffic resume, which it logged no errors handling [tr_f75ff8f53156]. product-catalog, checkout, recommendation and frontend-proxy are untouched by this action; if their alerts clear, that is evidence of a causal link that has not otherwise been established.
